sections.label: Mediation Act 2017 framework
sections.summary: The Mediation Act was enacted in 2017 to establish a mediation framework and a more conducive environment for international commercial mediation in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: For instance, the Mediation Act was enacted in 2017 to establish a framework for mediation, and to provide a more conducive environment in Singapore for international commercial mediation.

sections.label: UN adopts Singapore Convention
sections.summary: On 20 December 2018 the UN General Assembly adopted the Convention, authorised signing in Singapore and the name Singapore Convention on Mediation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: On 20 December 2018, the UN General Assembly, in a momentous decision, adopted the Convention.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: It also authorised the signing of the Convention to be held in Singapore and authorised the Convention to be known henceforth as the “Singapore Convention on Mediation”.

sections.label: Countries signing and attending
sections.summary: Forty-six countries signed the Convention on the day it opened for signature, and another 24 attended the signing ceremony to show support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Forty-six countries signed the Convention on the day it opened for signature, while another 24 countries attended the signing ceremony to show their support for the Convention.

sections.label: Six more signatories in New York
sections.summary: Six other countries later signed the Convention at UN headquarters in New York, bringing total signatories to 52.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Subsequently, six other countries signed onto the Convention at the UN headquarters in New York, bringing the total number of signatories to the Convention today to 52.

sections.label: Mediated settlement not directly enforceable
sections.summary: A mediated settlement agreement is contractually binding but is not itself directly enforceable in the Courts, unlike a Court judgment or arbitral award.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: While a mediated settlement agreement is contractually binding, it is not itself directly enforceable in the Courts, unlike a Court judgment or an arbitral award.

sections.label: Convention entry into force requirements
sections.summary: At least three states must deposit their instrument for the Convention to enter into force six months later, and Singapore aims to ratify among the first.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In order for the Convention and, therefore, this Bill to enter into force, at least three states must deposit their instrument of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Convention will enter into force six months after the third state deposits its instrument.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: On Singapore’s part, we aim to be amongst the first countries to ratify the Convention and will take steps to do so once this Bill is passed and Presidential Assent is obtained.

sections.label: Clause 9 and Convention reservations
sections.summary: Clause 9 lets a Court adjourn proceedings and order security for costs, and the Bill does not implement the Convention's two reservations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In clause 9, if there are parallel proceedings in another Court, tribunal or other competent authority, the Court hearing an application under the Bill may adjourn the hearing and order the other party to give suitable security for costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This Bill does not currently implement either of the two reservations allowed under the Convention.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The effect of this non-implementation of the reservation is that, firstly, the Convention and the Bill will apply to settlement agreements that the Government is a party to; and two, the Convention and the Bill will apply automatically to parties to a settlement agreement who may wish to enforce or invoke their agreement in a Singapore Court under the Convention.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Parties may, however, agree through the terms of their settlement agreement, to opt out of the Convention.

sections.label: Bill and mediation benefits
sections.summary: The Bill is expected to let more businesses benefit from mediation and strengthens Singapore's dispute resolution framework.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: With the introduction of the Convention, it is anticipated that more businesses will seek to avail themselves of the benefits that the mediation process provides, as adoption of the Convention becomes more prevalent globally.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This Bill is an essential instrument that will enable parties to benefit from the framework that is already set out in the Convention, and it is a significant step in our overall efforts to strengthen Singapore’s dispute resolution framework.

sections.label: Singapore Convention drafting and features
sections.summary: Singapore helped draft the Convention, which was opened for signature on 7 August 2019 and does not operate on reciprocity.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Singapore had a major role in drafting the document.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And what is more is that the Singapore Convention on Mediation was opened for signature on 7 August 2019, our Bicentennial year, and also named after us.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Reading through the Bill, there are some unique pointers unlike other multilateral enforcement regimes, such as that it does not operate based on reciprocity between member states.

sections.label: Query on mediated settlement enforcement
sections.summary: A member asks whether a settlement intended to result from mediation qualifies for enforcement regardless of place of origin.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Can I also clarify with the Senior Minister of State that as long as a settlement is intended and will result from mediation, then that commercial case will qualify for enforcement under the Convention, regardless of its place of origin or the nation of origin?

sections.label: Query on mediated agreement enforceability
sections.summary: A member asks whether an agreement arising from mediation will be enforceable with the passing of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Another query I have on this is: will an agreement arising from mediation now be enforceable with the passing of this Bill?

sections.label: Singapore Mediation Centre statistics
sections.summary: The Singapore Mediation Centre has mediated over 4,000 matters, with about a 70% settlement rate and over 90% resolved within a day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: At present, we have the Singapore Mediation Centre (SMC), which has mediated over 4,000 matters to date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The settlement rate is approximately 70%, with more than 90% of the settled disputes resolved within a day.

sections.label: Bill records mediated settlements as Court orders
sections.summary: The Bill lets international commercial settlement agreements be recorded as Court orders, enforceable like High Court judgments, unlike contractually binding mediated agreements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Under the new Bill, international commercial settlement agreements may be recorded as an order of Court which can then be more readily enforced in the same manner as a judgment by the High Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: This is an improvement from the long-standing position where mediated settlement agreements are typically only binding contractually between parties and not directly enforceable as a Court Order.

sections.label: SMC mediation cases concluded in one day
sections.summary: The SMC team shared that 90% of mediation cases are concluded within one day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The team at SMC has shared that 90% of mediation cases are concluded within one day.

sections.label: Singapore Convention on Mediation signatures
sections.summary: The Singapore Convention on Mediation, adopted 20 December 2018 and opened for signature 7 August 2019, governs recognition of mediated settlements and has been signed by 52 states.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Singapore Convention on Mediation, formally the UN Convention on International Settlement Agreements Resulting from Mediation which was adopted on 20 December 2018 and opened for signature on 7 August 2019, is an international agreement governing the recognition of mediated settlements across different countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The UN General Assembly adopted this agreement on 18 December 2018, and it is very heartening that the agreement has since been signed by 52 states since it was opened for signature.

sections.label: Firms keen on ASEAN expansion
sections.summary: In the Singapore Business Federation National Business Survey 2019/2020, 76% of firms intending to expand were keen on the ASEAN region, similar to 2018/2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the Singapore Business Federation National Business Survey 2019/2020, 76% of firms which indicated that they intended to expand were keen to venture into the ASEAN region, similar to 2018/2019 levels.

sections.label: Mediation in tripartite partnership and TADM
sections.summary: Mediation has long been the preferred dispute resolution tool in this tripartite partnership, especially since TADM was established in April 2017, with Minister Josephine Teo providing statistics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Within this tripartite partnership, mediation has long been the preferred tool to resolve disputes, especially since the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) was established in April 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In reply to a written question in Parliament in August last year by my fellow Nominated Member of Parliament, Ms Anthea Ong, Minister Josephine Teo provided statistics, which in my humble opinion, has shown TADM's commendable rates on successful settlements and enforcement.

sections.label: Trade associations to advocate mediation benefits
sections.summary: Trade Association Chambers must advocate and educate the business community on business legislation changes and mediation benefits, with work beginning once the Bill passes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As Trade Association Chambers, we need to be committed to advocate and educate the business community with the ongoing changes to business legislation and the subsequent benefits of mediation to companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Once this Bill is passed, I believe our work begins.

sections.label: Singapore Convention signatures and commencement
sections.summary: 70 countries attended the 2019 signing ceremony, 46 signed, five more later, totalling 51 signatures; it commences six months after the third ratification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: On 7 August 2019, 70 countries attended the signing ceremony of the Singapore Convention with a total of 46 signing it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Subsequently, another five states signed it, bringing the total current signatures to 51.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: While there are currently 51 signatures to the Singapore Convention, the Singapore Convention will only commence operations six months after the third ratification.

sections.label: Recording mediated settlement agreements
sections.summary: The Bill allows an international settlement agreement from mediation to be recorded in Singapore as a Court order for enforcement, defence, set-off or reliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What this Bill does is that it provides that an international settlement agreement formed through mediation of a dispute may be recorded in Singapore as a Court order for the purposes of enforcement or defence, set-off or otherwise rely on it in a Court proceeding.

sections.label: Clause 8 absent party provisions
sections.summary: Clause 8 does not require refusal for an absent party, allows setting aside on substantive grounds, and includes the Singapore Convention text in the schedule.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: But clause 8 does not require a Court to refuse to record a settlement agreement simply because the other party is absent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This prevents a person from running away from what he had agreed to in the mediation settlement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: On the other hand, to ensure that a mere procedural lapse will not prevent justice from being done, clause 8 allows for an order recorded in the absence of a party to be set aside on the application of the absent party based on substantive arguments, that is, grounds on which the Court may refuse to grant an application to record an order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This Bill also includes the entire text of the Singapore Convention in the schedule.

sections.label: SMUSIMI Collaborative Dispute Resolution Award
sections.summary: The award recognises law students from SMU, NUS and SUSS who excelled in international collaborative dispute resolution competitions or contributed to mediation and negotiation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, the "National SMUSIMI Collaborative Dispute Resolution Award" recognises law students from the local universities – Singapore Management University (SMU), National University of Singapore (NUS) and Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) – who have excelled in international collaborative dispute resolution competitions or who have contributed significantly to the mediation and negotiation in Singapore.

sections.label: Serious breach by mediator
sections.summary: Proposed section 7(2)(e) provides that an international settlement agreement may be enforced if the mediator seriously breached applicable mediator or mediation standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The proposed section 7(2)(e) provides that an international settlement agreement may be enforced if “there was a serious breach by the mediator who conducted the mediation that resulted in the international settlement agreement of the standards applicable to the mediator, or the mediation”.

sections.label: Mediator standards self-regulation question
sections.summary: The question asks whether there are plans for industry self-regulation of mediator standards or for MinLaw to consolidate a single set of mediation standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State share if there are plans to leave the industry to self-regulate in determining the applicable mediator standards or if the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) intends to take the lead in consolidating a single set of mediation standards?

sections.label: Guidance on serious breach definition
sections.summary: The Senior Minister of State is asked whether the Ministry plans guidance on what constitutes a serious breach or leaves it to Courts and mediation institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State share whether there are plans for the Ministry to provide guidance on what should constitute "serious breach" or will the definition be left entirely up to the Courts and mediation institutions?

sections.label: Review of civil enforcement procedures
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked whether its review of civil enforcement procedures will affect processes under the current Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share whether this review of civil enforcement procedures will affect the processes under this current Bill?

sections.label: Three states ratifying Convention
sections.summary: Three states must ratify the Convention before it becomes effective six months after the third deposits its instrument with the UN.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As I outlined earlier, we require three states to ratify the Convention before the Convention becomes effective six months after the third state has deposited its instrument of ratification with the UN.

sections.label: Singapore Convention Conference September 2020
sections.summary: The next Singapore Convention Conference is scheduled in Singapore in September 2020, with a Singapore Convention Week of events.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The next Singapore Convention Conference is scheduled to be held in Singapore in September 2020, in conjunction with a Singapore Convention Week of events.

sections.label: Expected increase in mediated disputes
sections.summary: With a framework simplifying enforcement of international settlement agreements, more disputes are expected to be resolved under the Bill and Domestic Mediation Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: With the introduction of a framework to simplify the process for enforcement and invocation of international settlement agreements, we do expect to see an increase in the number of disputes resolved in accordance with this Bill, and slowly, with the proliferation of mediation, increasingly as a viable option for resolving disputes, and also under the Domestic Mediation Act.

sections.label: Disjunctive limbs cover administered mediations
sections.summary: The clause's disjunctive limbs mean the Bill covers administered and unadministered mediations, with institutional attestation only one way to evidence a settlement agreement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: There are several limbs to the clause and they are all disjunctive.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Hence, the Bill caters to both administered and unadministered mediations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Clause 6(1)(b)(ii), for instance, provides that an attestation by the institution that administered the mediation is only one of the ways in which a settlement agreement can be evidenced to have resulted from a mediation.

sections.label: SIMC international mediator panel
sections.summary: SIMC's panel has about 70 international mediators from over 20 jurisdictions with civil and common law backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: SIMC’s panel has about 70 international mediators from more than 20 jurisdictions across a spectrum of civil and common law backgrounds.

sections.label: SIMC specialist training workshop
sections.summary: In November last year, SIMC held a two-day specialist training workshop for 24 senior Singapore practitioners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Recently, in November last year, SIMC conducted a two-day specialist training workshop for 24 senior practitioners from Singapore.

sections.label: Stakeholders welcomed the Bill
sections.summary: Stakeholders consulted, including the legal fraternity, dispute resolution institutions and businesses, welcomed the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Stakeholders, including the legal fraternity, dispute resolution institutions, businesses that we consulted, welcomed the Bill.

sections.label: Commercial international agreements enforceable
sections.summary: Once passed and in force, commercial and international agreements meeting the Bill's requirements will be enforceable under its framework.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: When the Bill is passed and enters into force, agreements which are of a commercial and international in nature, and which fulfil the requirements of the Bill, will be enforceable under the Bill's framework.

sections.label: Party chooses Convention jurisdiction
sections.summary: A party can choose which jurisdiction to bring an application under the Convention, provided that jurisdiction is a party to it.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The answer to Prof Fatimah Lateef's question is yes and, indeed, that is the value behind the Convention.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: A party can choose which jurisdiction it wishes to bring an application under the Convention, provided that the jurisdiction is a party to the Convention.

sections.label: Convention excludes family inheritance employment
sections.summary: The Convention the Bill seeks to implement excludes disputes relating to family, inheritance or employment law.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Convention, which the Bill seeks to implement, itself excludes disputes in relation to "family, inheritance or employment law".

sections.label: Bill covers mediation settlement agreements
sections.summary: The Bill covers all settlement agreements from mediations to resolve a commercial dispute.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Bill covers all settlement agreements from mediations to resolve a commercial dispute.

sections.label: Applications to High Court or Court of Appeal
sections.summary: In Singapore, applications under the Bill are made to the High Court or Court of Appeal, as appropriate.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In Singapore, applications under the Bill are to be made to the High Court or to the Court of Appeal, as appropriate.

sections.label: Onus on applicant to prove requirements
sections.summary: The party seeking to make an application under the Bill must prove the settlement agreement resulted from mediation and conditions were complied with.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The onus is on the party seeking to make an application under the Bill to prove that requirements under clause 6(1)(b), which I have mentioned a little while ago, that the settlement agreement resulted from mediation, and that these conditions have been complied with.

sections.label: No upfront standards for mediators
sections.summary: Neither the Convention nor the Bill sets out upfront, immutable standards for the mediator or mediation, and no plans exist to impose a regulatory regime on mediators for the time being.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Accordingly, neither the Convention nor the Bill sets out standards that are prescribed upfront and become immutable over time, applying to the mediator or to the mediation itself.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We are about six months out from the Convention.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We do not currently have plans to impose a regulatory regime on mediators for the time being.

sections.label: Courts determine applicable standards and breach
sections.summary: Applicable standards based on licensing, party agreement, or institution rules, and whether there has been a serious breach, are determined by the Courts hearing an application under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To the extent that there are, in fact, such "applicable" standards based on the mediator’s licensing regime, due to the parties’ agreement with the mediator, or pursuant to the rules of an administering institution, these standards, and consequently, whether there has been a "serious breach" or not, are to be determined by the competent authority hearing an application under the Bill, in other words, the Courts.
